title: The letter repeats an octave higher
summary: Match a string with its twelfth fret.

steps.title: The higher version
steps.body:
An **octave** is the distance of twelve half steps. At fret 12 a string has the same letter name as its open sound, but sounds higher. The small number in A2 or A3 tells you which height to play.

**Why it matters:** Matching a letter alone is not enough when a question asks for an exact sound: A2 and A3 are different notes.

steps.title: Two As, different heights
steps.body: Hear A2 followed by A3. You can also find A3 at fret 7 on string 4 or fret 2 on string 3. All positions for A3 count; A2 is too low for an A3 question.

items.prompt: Play A3. Use any lit position.

steps.title: Compare open and twelve
steps.body: Pluck any open string, then fret 12 on that string. Hear the matching letter higher up. If fret 12 is uncomfortable, use the on-screen fretboard.

items.prompt: How far apart are these two notes?
